title: X-MoE: Enabling Scalable Training for Emerging Mixture-of-Experts Architectures on HPC Platforms
problem: Emerging expert-specialized Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures like DeepSeek-MoE have substantial activation memory overhead and costly all-to-all communication, limiting scalability. Current systems are optimized for NVIDIA GPUs and perform suboptimally on other platforms.
motivation: MoE architectures deliver superior model quality through fine-grained expert segmentation and large top-k routing, but their training is computationally demanding and platform-specific, limiting adoption on diverse HPC systems.
method: X-MoE scales mixture-of-experts training (a neural network approach where different experts activate based on input) through three optimizations: memory-efficient code that runs on different hardware platforms, direct expert routing that eliminates redundant data copying, and hybrid parallelization that splits both the data and model across machines. Together, these reduce memory overhead and communication bottlenecks that normally limit the size of models you can train.
key_novelty: X-MoE is a mixture-of-experts training system that eliminates wasted memory space and redundant data routing, enabling models 10x larger than existing methods across diverse hardware including AMD GPUs.
contributions: Trains DeepSeek-style MoEs up to 545 billion parameters on 1024 GPUs (Frontier)
10x larger than models trainable with existing methods under same hardware budget
limitations: Full-text not available; analysis based on abstract. Evaluation primarily on Frontier; generalization to other HPC systems not discussed. Throughput metrics not provided.
primary_theme: Cross-platform scalable MoE training for HPC systems
